title: Church singing, the ukulele and street-corner quartets
summary: His mother sang in the AME choir; he played ukulele and sang baritone in a street-corner quartet.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: When do you get interested though in music?
Well, I used -- before I left -- I used to -- I think after I came back -- after I came back to -- say -- buried my brother and my mother more or less -- Well, my mother was in the church.
A Holiness Church or a Baptist Church?
AME Church. And, she used to sing alot. She sang in the choir, and I used to sing along with her at home, you know.
Did she have a pretty voice?
Oh Yeah. And, then I used to play the ukelele.
When you were still a kid?
I don't remember how I got it (laugh). I really don't.
Somebody maybe had one and you --
Well, ukeleles were real popular weren't they?
Yes. Yeah. I don't remember. I don't remember.
And you used to sing? Sing along?
Yeah. And then they used to sing on corners like quartets, you know what I mean. We used to get together --
-- and sing on corners. And I used to sing Irish songs. It was four voices in other words, and I used to be more or less the baritone singer I sang baritone.
Yeah. With a harmony -- the barbershop.
And you'd pick up some nickels and dimes?
What would you do -- hold out a hat or?
No, no. We didn't go in for that. And I was the youngest in the group more or less, you know what I mean? And these guys were bigger than me.
But I had the voice that they needed so I --
Just at night, just for our own amusement. -- get out and just
Perform. You did? You'd just perform.
Yeah. You know. Just -- that's all.
So that was your first taste of music, right?
